tools.name: search_items
tools.description: Search library items. All filters are optional and combine with AND. With NO filters, `total_matches` is the exact count of all non-trashed items in the library — use that for "how many items" questions. `query` matches name, link title/description, tags, annotation, author, location, and source URL, case-insensitively — it reads METADATA only, so for "find pictures of X" use search_by_description, which matches what items actually show. Scope with `collection`, `collection_folder`, `smart_folder`, `connected_folder`, or `source` (instagram / x). Filter by kind, tags (all / any), format, size, dimensions, duration, orientation, liked, untagged, date ranges (ISO 8601). Sort by date_added (default), date_created, name, bytes, duration, width, height, or random. Trashed items are excluded unless you search `collection: "Trash"`. For library-wide totals (how many images / videos / items) library_info answers in one cheap call. Enum filters accept "" for "no filter"; 0 on an optional number also means "not set". Returns compact metadata; `verbose: true` adds paths, notes and file facts; use view_items to actually see items.

tools.description: Find items by what they SHOW, from a plain-language description — "a red sports car at night", "hand-drawn arrow sketch", "brutalist concrete facade". Atlas embeds the description on this Mac with the same model that indexed every thumbnail, and returns the closest items, best first, each with a cosine `score`. Reach for this whenever the request is about what's IN the picture rather than what it's called: search_items only matches names, tags, notes and URLs, so it misses everything nobody happened to label. Narrow with `kind` / `collection`. Colors and preview-less links are never indexed. Pass the ids to show_items to put the results on the user's screen. Needs Settings ▸ General ▸ "Semantic search" on; the first query after launch loads the text model and can take a few seconds.
tools.name: search_by_description

tools.description: Store semantic-embedding vectors for library items, keyed by `content_hash` (from search_items / get_item file facts). `model` names the embedding model that produced them (e.g. "siglip2-base-patch16-256") — vectors from different models don't mix, so storing under a new model id DISCARDS the previously stored index. Vectors are L2-normalized on the way in and persisted with the library. Send items in batches (max 1000 per call). Entries whose hash is unknown to the library are still stored (the item may sync in later); use `prune: true` on a final batch to drop vectors whose hash no longer matches any item.

entries.description: Vectors to store, keyed by the item's content_hash

prune.description: Afterwards, drop stored vectors whose hash matches no current item

model.description: Embedding model id these vectors came from

query_embeddings
tools.description: Semantic search over the vectors stored with store_embeddings, for clients that bring their own model: pass a query vector (a text or image embedding from the SAME model) and get the closest items back, best first, scored by cosine similarity. To search Atlas's own on-device index from plain language — no model needed — use search_by_description instead. Trashed items are excluded. With no vector, returns index status only (model, count, dimension). Combine with select_items / show_in_app to surface the hits in the Atlas window.

min_score.description: Drop results whose cosine falls below this (model-specific scale)

vector.description: Query embedding (same model + dimension as the stored vectors)

model.description: Embedding model id the query vector came from

tools.description: Library housekeeping. `remove_duplicates` runs File ▸ Clean up library: byte-identical files collapse onto one stored copy, a collection holding several keeps one entry (an item left in no collection goes to the Trash), and every other copy stays in place as a virtual copy, deleting the freed files; `remove_missing_originals` forgets items whose files are gone from disk; `purge_expired_trash` deletes trashed items older than `days`.
